# Classical music: who composed it? — provenance report

<!-- Generated from authored/classical-music-composers.json by scripts/authored_decks.py. Do not edit: change the dossier and rebuild. -->

**Deck:** [`decks/classical-music-composers.ttl`](../decks/classical-music-composers.ttl) · **Cards:** 83 · **Licence:** [CC0 1.0 Universal](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/) · **Compiled by:** Anton Wiklund · **Created:** 2026-10-04

83 famous works of Western classical music composed before 1950 – operas, ballets and concert works chosen by how many Wikimedia sites (mostly language editions of Wikipedia) have a page on them. Front: the work's title in English and Swedish (where a title has been used for several works, the best-known one is meant); back: its composer. Titles and composers from Wikidata, checked against the Library of Congress name authorities and IMSLP.

## Licensing

The deck is CC0 1.0. Everything in the cards — the choice of works, the titles, the composers and their names, and the namesakes named in back notes — comes from Wikidata, whose structured data is CC0, or is our own wording (the back notes, 'Eroica Symphony', and Swedish titles that are common names checked in Swedish Wikipedia, such as 'Jupitersymfonin', 'Uvertyren 1812' and 'Triptyken'). The selection is our own: a ranking by Wikidata's sitelink counts with the stated exclusions, not a list taken from any publication. The Library of Congress Name Authority File (a public-domain data set) and IMSLP (wiki pages CC BY-SA 4.0) were used only to confirm composers and namesakes, and Swedish and English Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0) only to confirm titles and what kind of work a namesake is; no text or selection was copied from them, so their share-alike terms do not reach the deck. Facts such as who composed a work or what a work is called are not copyrightable.

## Method

1. Who did the work: the research, drafting and cross-checking were done by AI agents (Claude, by Anthropic) at Anton Wiklund's direction, with independent AI reviewers (factual accuracy, language, licensing and documentation, and a final re-check; see Quality control) and machine checks (the builder's Wikidata checks and the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators). The cards have not yet been reviewed by a human subject expert.
2. Candidates (Wikidata, 2026-10-04): every Wikidata item with a composer statement (P86) and at least 25 sitelinks, from the Wikidata Query Service (query 1). wikibase:sitelinks counts the item's pages on every Wikimedia project: mostly the language editions of Wikipedia, but also Wikiquote, Wikisource, Wikinews and Commons; the whole selection ranks by this count, not by Wikipedia articles alone. This returned 9,616 rows for 8,262 items, most of them films, TV series and anthems.
3. Details: for the 8,262 items, in batches of 300, the English and Swedish labels, the composer and the composer's English label and date of death, the item's classes (P31) and the earliest inception (P571), publication date (P577) and date of first performance (P1191) (query 2).
4. Filter (a Python script over the saved results): a work was kept when its earliest P571/P577/P1191 date is before 1950 — or, with none of those dates, when every composer died before 1950 — and when its classes include musical work/composition (Q105543609), dramatico-musical work (Q58483083), ballet (Q58483088), passion (Q781815) or one of the other music classes listed in the filter under Queries, but none of film, animated film, short film, TV series, animated series or national anthem. The remaining works were ranked by sitelink count (all Wikimedia projects).
5. Editorial screening of the ranked list from the top, by the criteria in Selection: songs, carols, hymns, chant, anthems, patriotic and military songs and marches, musicals and plays with music were set aside as not Western classical concert, opera or ballet repertoire; numbered works without an established nickname (e.g. Beethoven's Symphony No. 9, Mozart's Requiem) were set aside as generic titles. Every work at or above the cut that was set aside is listed in Selection.
6. Title clashes: for the shortlisted works, query 3 found every other Wikidata item with a composer whose English or Swedish label is exactly the same as the work's label in that language. A work was dropped when a same-titled musical work by another composer has at least half as many sitelinks (this removed Verdi's Otello, 45 sitelinks, against Rossini's Otello with 26). Query 3 compared labels only, so after review (quality-control round 3) query 4 repeated the search with the titles actually on the card fronts, in each language, matched against the labels and the aliases of every item with a composer. Namesakes that are films, TV series, video games, theatre productions or popular songs were ignored. Every other namesake (an opera, operetta, musical, ballet or concert work by another composer) with at least 5 sitelinks is named in a back note that says which work is meant: Aida, Turandot, The Barber of Seville, La bohème, Manon Lescaut, Falstaff, Faust, Macbeth, Salome, Boléro, Pastoral Symphony, Orfeo ed Euridice and L'Orfeo. A few less-known namesakes are named too (Ferdinando Bertoni, Antonio Sartorio); the others with fewer than 5 sitelinks are not (e.g. Galuppi's and Federici's Idomeneo, Prokofiev's film music The Queen of Spades, Strauss II's quadrille Un ballo in maschera, Balfe's Falstaff). Works with a different title (e.g. Suppé's Pique Dame) are outside this check. Query 4 found no new clash under the drop rule: the only musical namesake with more than half a card's sitelinks, Massenet's Manon (29, against Manon Lescaut's 40), matched only through its Swedish alias 'Manon Lescaut'; its title is Manon, so the card stays and its back note names Massenet's opera. Every namesake named in a note is cited on the card with its Wikidata item and has a composer (P86) check.
7. The deck takes the eligible works in sitelink order down to 35 sitelinks, with the whole of the tie at 35, which gives 83 cards (the brief asked for about 80).
8. Titles: the English front is Wikidata's English label, or an English alias where the label is a generic numbered title (Moonlight Sonata, Pastoral Symphony, Sonata Pathétique, Jupiter Symphony, Canon in D); 'Eroica Symphony' is our own English form of the alias 'Eroica'. La traviata has no English or Swedish label in Wikidata, only a multilingual ('mul') label 'La traviata'; the builder's label checks accept a mul label. The Swedish front is Wikidata's Swedish label or alias, except where that is missing or would mislead; then the title of the Swedish Wikipedia article (a sitelink in Wikidata) or a Swedish form checked in Swedish Wikipedia's text was used: La traviata, La bohème, Symphonie fantastique, Spader dam, Sonata Pathétique, Jupitersymfonin, L'Orfeo (Swedish Wikipedia's redirect title for Monteverdi's opera, whose article opens 'Orfeo (italienska: L'Orfeo …)'; Wikidata's Swedish label 'Orfeus' is also the name of the mythical singer, and the bare 'Orfeo' is Wikidata's Swedish label of Luigi Rossi's opera) and Uvertyren 1812 (Wikidata's Swedish label is just '1812', which would read as a year; its Swedish alias 'Ouvertyren 1812', used at first, was not found in Swedish Wikipedia's text, which has 'Uvertyren 1812'). Swedish Wikipedia's text was read for those cards and for the Swedish titles that differ from the original-language title in a way a Swedish reader might question (Nebukadnessar, Ragnarök, Valkyrian, Rhenguldet, Läderlappen, Trubaduren, Eroica, Pastoralsymfonin, Månskenssonaten, Kanon i D, Törnrosa, Wilhelm Tell). Titles are tagged with the language in whose usage they are the established title, even when the title itself is in the original language (German, Italian, Latin or French): e.g. 'Der Ring des Nibelungen'@en, 'Das wohltemperierte Klavier'@sv, 'Così fan tutte'@en and @sv; Wikidata's English and Swedish labels follow the same practice.
9. Composers: the back is the composer from Wikidata P86 (every selected work has exactly one). The name is Wikidata's English label (one exception: for Gluck, the back uses 'Christoph Willibald Gluck', an English alias, the Swedish label and the title of the English and Swedish Wikipedia articles, rather than the English label 'Christoph Willibald von Gluck'); where Wikidata's Swedish label spells the name differently (transliterated Russian names, Handel/Händel, Rossini's Gioachino/Gioacchino, Leoncavallo's Ruggero/Ruggiero, the Strausses' II/I against d.y./d.ä.) the back gives the English and the Swedish form, tagged; otherwise the name is untagged.
10. Cross-check: for each work, its Library of Congress authority id (Wikidata P244) was looked up and the LC record fetched from id.loc.gov (…/authorities/names/<id>.madsrdf.json); the LC authorized heading begins with the composer's name and dates. For the 12 works with no usable LC heading (no P244, or for Giselle a heading without the composer) the IMSLP work page was found through the IMSLP API; IMSLP page titles end with the composer's name; the title cited is the one the page shows after any redirect. Every card's composer agreed with its second source.
11. Machine checks: every card has Wikidata checks run by the builder: the composer (P86), the English and Swedish front titles as a label or alias where they are one, and the composer's name as a label in each language used. Label checks were left out only where the card's title is not a Wikidata label or alias, as listed in quality control.
12. Back notes were written by us from the evidence listed on each card: Wikidata namesake items (each with a composer check), Library of Congress headings showing a work as part of a larger one, and Swedish Wikipedia for the Swedish title of a larger work (Triptyken). IMSLP page lists and English Wikipedia only confirm what Wikidata gives.
13. Dates in the evidence: each Wikidata entry gives the work's earliest inception (P571), publication (P577) or first performance (P1191) at year precision or finer. Sixteen works also have a coarser value, a publication date of 1850 with century precision ('19th century'); the evidence says so, since Wikidata does not date them 1850 (quality-control round 3). Four works have none of these dates in Wikidata and passed the filter only through its fallback, the composer's death before 1950: canon-in-d (Pachelbel, died 1706), goldberg-variations and brandenburg-concertos (Bach, died 1750) and nessun-dorma (Puccini, died 1924); their evidence says this instead of giving a work date (quality-control round 5). Alias lists in the evidence are the aliases seen at retrieval and are given as 'aliases include', since Wikidata's alias lists change. No date is shown on a card.

## Selection

Included: the 83 highest-ranked works by Wikidata sitelink count (pages on all Wikimedia projects, mostly Wikipedias; Wikidata, 2026-10-04) among musical works with a single named composer, dated (inception, publication or first performance) before 1950, that belong to the Western classical opera, ballet, concert or church-music repertoire and have a title that identifies them on its own. The cut is at 35 sitelinks, with the whole tie at 35. Because the count includes Wikiquote, Wikisource, Wikinews and Commons, 11 of the 83 works have fewer than 35 Wikipedia articles (Sonata Pathétique has 32 of its 35 sitelinks on Wikipedias); a ranking by Wikipedia articles alone would give a slightly different list. Excluded: every work that passed the filter with at least 35 sitelinks but is not in the deck, all 30 of them (Wikidata item, sitelinks): songs, carols, hymns and chant — The Internationale (Q49617, 133), Stille Nacht (Q172152, 79), Auld Lang Syne (Q211939, 55), Happy Birthday to You (Q167545, 53), 'O Sole Mio (Q205891, 50), Jingle Bells (Q406845, 48), Hava Nagila (Q131718, 47), Salve Regina (Q301934, 45), Waltzing Matilda (Q752873, 40), La Espero (Q141005, 38), Greensleeves (Q674738, 37), Bogurodzica (Q890692, 37); national, patriotic and military songs and marches — Katyusha (Q18288, 58), Rule, Britannia! (Q215729, 40), Farewell of Slavianka (Q331969, 39), Erika (Q700867, 37), The Sacred War (Q714119, 37); popular songs — Bésame Mucho (Q391180, 45), Gloomy Sunday (Q747869, 42), Over the Rainbow (Q161402, 40), You'll Never Walk Alone (Q728692, 38), White Christmas (Q1131761, 37), Lili Marleen (Q154968, 37); a play with music — The Threepenny Opera (Q212495, 46); generic numbered titles without an established nickname in both languages — Beethoven's Symphony No. 9 (Q11989, 65), Symphony No. 5 (Q188709, 56) and Symphony No. 1 (Q163493, 35), Mozart's Symphony No. 40 (Q231390, 35) and Mozart's Requiem (Q207875, 51; a generic title, and Wikidata also names Franz Xaver Süssmayr as its composer); and Verdi's Otello (Q172324, 45), whose title is shared with Rossini's Otello. The Radetzky March is kept as an orchestral concert piece by Johann Strauss I, though it is a march; this is a judgement call. Arias and parts with their own Wikidata item and rank (Nessun dorma; the four operas of the Ring) are kept as works in their own right. Sitelink counts change over time, so a re-run of the queries may give a slightly different list.

## Queries

**1. Candidates: items with a composer and at least 25 sitelinks (https://query.wikidata.org/sparql). A first version that also fetched labels, dates and classes in one query timed out (HTTP 504), so the details were fetched separately in query 2** (Wikidata)

```
SELECT ?work ?sl ?composer WHERE {
  ?work wdt:P86 ?composer ;
        wikibase:sitelinks ?sl .
  FILTER(?sl >= 25)
}
```

**2. Details for the candidates, run in batches of 300 item ids substituted for %s (https://query.wikidata.org/sparql)** (Wikidata)

```
SELECT ?work ?sl ?enLabel ?svLabel ?composer ?composerLabel ?composerDeath
  (GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT ?type; separator="|") AS ?types)
  (MIN(?inc) AS ?inception) (MIN(?pub) AS ?publication) (MIN(?prem) AS ?premiere) WHERE {
  VALUES ?work { %s }
  ?work wdt:P86 ?composer ; wikibase:sitelinks ?sl .
  OPTIONAL { ?work rdfs:label ?enLabel . FILTER(LANG(?enLabel) = "en") }
  OPTIONAL { ?work rdfs:label ?svLabel . FILTER(LANG(?svLabel) = "sv") }
  OPTIONAL { ?composer rdfs:label ?composerLabel . FILTER(LANG(?composerLabel) = "en") }
  OPTIONAL { ?composer wdt:P570 ?composerDeath . }
  OPTIONAL { ?work wdt:P31 ?type . }
  OPTIONAL { ?work wdt:P571 ?inc . }
  OPTIONAL { ?work wdt:P577 ?pub . }
  OPTIONAL { ?work wdt:P1191 ?prem . }
}
GROUP BY ?work ?sl ?enLabel ?svLabel ?composer ?composerLabel ?composerDeath
```

**Filter applied to the results of query 2 (Python, scratch script filter.py)** (Wikidata)

```
date = earliest of P571, P577, P1191; if none: the latest composer death date, when every composer has one
keep if date < 1950
  and P31 includes one of Q105543609 Q58483083 Q58483088 Q781815 Q15079786 Q2188189 Q207628
  and P31 includes none of Q11424 Q202866 Q24862 Q17517379 Q5398426 Q117467246 Q23691 Q1259759 Q63952888 Q113791292 Q196600 Q15416 Q7058673 Q116476516
sort by sitelinks, descending
```

**Labels, aliases, Wikipedia sitelink titles and composers of the shortlisted works (Wikidata API, 50 ids per request)** (Wikidata)

```
https://www.wikidata.org/w/api.php?action=wbgetentities&ids=<ids joined by |>&props=labels|aliases|sitelinks|claims&languages=en|sv|mul&sitefilter=enwiki|svwiki&format=json
```

**3. Same-titled works by other composers (https://query.wikidata.org/sparql)** (Wikidata)

```
SELECT ?work ?lang ?title ?other ?otherSitelinks ?otherComposer ?otherComposerLabel WHERE {
  VALUES ?work { wd:Q185968 wd:Q5064 wd:Q171277 wd:Q186162 wd:Q19005 wd:Q199786 wd:Q201873 wd:Q192039 wd:Q192941 wd:Q189234 wd:Q11980 wd:Q12016 wd:Q190237 wd:Q193705 wd:Q202230 wd:Q207990 wd:Q1324254 wd:Q208659 wd:Q188621 wd:Q193778 wd:Q203470 wd:Q207410 wd:Q221806 wd:Q206015 wd:Q248644 wd:Q253716 wd:Q172324 wd:Q207732 wd:Q211971 wd:Q212776 wd:Q220340 wd:Q23085 wd:Q482621 wd:Q50956 wd:Q157489 wd:Q179110 wd:Q327331 wd:Q212451 wd:Q12008 wd:Q221757 wd:Q114640 wd:Q156435 wd:Q324319 wd:Q12025 wd:Q213728 wd:Q327717 wd:Q462313 wd:Q827436 wd:Q244209 wd:Q560619 wd:Q208224 wd:Q221047 wd:Q246433 wd:Q272029 wd:Q320353 wd:Q723407 wd:Q12001 wd:Q210711 wd:Q332536 wd:Q335012 wd:Q379111 wd:Q464930 wd:Q815342 wd:Q831852 wd:Q465540 wd:Q471240 wd:Q478202 wd:Q548161 wd:Q689519 wd:Q907745 wd:Q146113 wd:Q232367 wd:Q723559 wd:Q727868 wd:Q844790 wd:Q210549 wd:Q35720 wd:Q722599 wd:Q723941 wd:Q729568 wd:Q211279 wd:Q333146 wd:Q838051 wd:Q176700 wd:Q745951 wd:Q459341 wd:Q318455 wd:Q723776 wd:Q724008 wd:Q729659 wd:Q320363 wd:Q767249 wd:Q578526 wd:Q911487 wd:Q14912776 wd:Q171405 wd:Q1239463 wd:Q831255 wd:Q1053812 wd:Q45784 wd:Q378237 wd:Q875563 wd:Q211460 wd:Q11985 wd:Q386846 wd:Q392734 }
  VALUES ?lang { "en" "sv" }
  ?work rdfs:label ?title . FILTER(LANG(?title) = ?lang)
  ?other rdfs:label ?title ; wdt:P86 ?otherComposer ; wikibase:sitelinks ?otherSitelinks .
  FILTER(?other != ?work)
  FILTER NOT EXISTS { ?work wdt:P86 ?otherComposer }
  OPTIONAL { ?otherComposer rdfs:label ?otherComposerLabel . FILTER(LANG(?otherComposerLabel) = "en") }
}
ORDER BY ?work
```

**4. Namesakes of the card fronts as used, labels and aliases (quality-control round 3; https://query.wikidata.org/sparql). ## Quality control

6 rounds, 42 findings: 36 fixed, 0 rejected after checking, 6 needing no change. Every card's Wikidata checks (429 in all) are re-run against live Wikidata by `scripts/authored_decks.py check` before every build.

### Round 0: Machine checks against Wikidata, a second source for every composer, and the Swedish titles (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — authoring agent, machine checks · **Scope:** All 83 cards

Every card's composer was confirmed by a Library of Congress heading or an IMSLP work page; no disagreement on who composed a work was found. The builder's Wikidata checks cover the composer (P86) of every card, the composer's name in each language used, and the front titles where they are a Wikidata label or alias. Title label checks were left out for: la-boheme (sv "La bohème"); eroica-symphony (en "Eroica Symphony"); symphonie-fantastique (sv "Symphonie fantastique"); the-queen-of-spades (sv "Spader dam"); sonata-pathetique (sv "Sonata Pathétique"); jupiter-symphony (sv "Jupitersymfonin"); l-orfeo (sv "L'Orfeo"); 1812-overture (sv "Uvertyren 1812"). Differences in name forms and titles between the sources are recorded below. (This list gives the final state after quality-control rounds 1 and 2, which changed the Swedish fronts of l-orfeo from 'Orfeo' to 'L'Orfeo' and of 1812-overture from 'Ouvertyren 1812' to 'Uvertyren 1812'; neither is a Wikidata Swedish label or alias; corrected in round 4.)

| Card | Issue | Resolution | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| the-queen-of-spades | Wikidata's Swedish label is 'Spader Dam'; the Swedish Wikipedia article title and later text use 'Spader dam', which follows Swedish capitalisation of titles. | Used 'Spader dam'; no Swedish label check for this card. | fixed |
| l-orfeo | Wikidata's Swedish label 'Orfeus' is also the name of the mythical singer; Swedish Wikipedia's article is 'Orfeo (opera, Monteverdi)' and says 'Orfeo (italienska: L'Orfeo …)'. | Used 'Orfeo' as the Swedish front; no Swedish label check. Superseded in rounds 1-2: the Swedish front is now "L'Orfeo", with no Swedish label check. | fixed |
| la-boheme | Wikidata's Swedish label is 'Bohème'; the Swedish Wikipedia article is titled 'La bohème'. | Used 'La bohème' in both languages; no Swedish label check. | fixed |
| 1812-overture | Wikidata's Swedish label is just '1812', which as a front would read as a year. | Used Wikidata's Swedish alias 'Ouvertyren 1812' (checked). Superseded in round 2: the Swedish front is now 'Uvertyren 1812', as in Swedish Wikipedia's text, with no Swedish label check. | fixed |
| nabucco | Considered using 'Nabucco' in Swedish too; Swedish Wikipedia says the opera is in Sweden mostly known as Nebukadnessar, which is Wikidata's Swedish label. | Kept 'Nebukadnessar' with a back note giving the Italian title. | no change needed |
| pagliacci | Name form: Wikidata's English label is 'Ruggero Leoncavallo'; the LC heading and Wikidata's Swedish label have 'Ruggiero'. | Both forms are in use; the back gives 'Ruggero Leoncavallo' (en) and 'Ruggiero Leoncavallo' (sv), each checked against Wikidata. | no change needed |
| the-barber-of-seville | Name form: Wikidata's English label is 'Gioachino Rossini'; the LC heading (for William Tell) and Wikidata's Swedish label have 'Gioacchino'; IMSLP has pages under both spellings. | The back gives 'Gioachino Rossini' (en) and 'Gioacchino Rossini' (sv). | no change needed |
| giselle | The LC heading for Giselle (n97822081) is 'Giselle (Choreographic work)' and does not name the composer. | Composer confirmed with the IMSLP page 'Giselle (Adam, Adolphe)' instead. | fixed |
| swan-lake | Wikidata gives two LC ids; sh2015001789 is not in the names file (HTTP 404 at id.loc.gov/authorities/names). | Used n81019548, 'Tchaikovsky, Peter Ilich, 1840-1893. Lebedinoe ozero'. | fixed |
| radetzky-march | Two composers named Johann Strauss: the LC headings separate them by dates (1804-1849 for the Radetzky March, 1825-1899 for The Blue Danube and Die Fledermaus), in agreement with Wikidata (Q184178 and Q83309). | Backs give 'Johann Strauss I' / 'Johann Strauss d.ä.' and 'Johann Strauss II' / 'Johann Strauss d.y.'. | no change needed |
| carmen | Some Wikidata dates are coarse: for several operas (e.g. Carmen, Rigoletto, Pagliacci, La bohème) the earliest of the inception/publication/first-performance values is 1850. For Carmen this is a publication date (P577) of 1850 with century precision (precision 7, i.e. the 19th century), beside an inception of 1875. | Dates were used only for the before-1950 filter, which every selected work passes on any of its dates; no date is shown on a card. | no change needed |
| eroica-symphony | The brief's example of a nickname title; Wikidata has the English alias 'Eroica' but not 'Eroica Symphony'. | English front 'Eroica Symphony' (our wording of the alias), no English label check; Swedish 'Eroica' is the Wikidata Swedish label and the Swedish Wikipedia title. | no change needed |

### Round 1: Factual accuracy (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — independent Factual accuracy reviewer · **Scope:** All 83 cards: each composer checked against the opening of the work's English Wikipedia article and the reviewer's own knowledge; the builder's 408 Wikidata checks re-run; the selection compared with an independent query of works with 35 or more sitelinks.

No wrong composer and no wrong back note. Two warnings: the Swedish front 'Orfeo' on l-orfeo was ambiguous (Gluck's opera, Luigi Rossi's Orfeo) and lacked a namesake note, and the deck described its ranking as Wikipedia coverage although wikibase:sitelinks counts all Wikimedia projects. Three suggestions: inconsistent namesake notes, a note for Vaughan Williams's Pastoral Symphony, and the Gluck name form. All were checked against Wikidata and Wikipedia and resolved; the namesake check was redone for the card fronts as used (query 4) with one rule for all notes.

| Card | Issue | Resolution | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| l-orfeo | The Swedish front 'Orfeo' does not point to one work: Gluck's Orfeo ed Euridice (in this deck) is often called just Orfeo, and 'Orfeo' is Wikidata's Swedish label of Luigi Rossi's opera (Q1118131). Antonio Sartorio's 'L'Orfeo' (Q7101699) was in the author's namesake data but the card had no back note. | Confirmed: Q1118131 has the English and Swedish label 'Orfeo' (composer Luigi Rossi, 7 sitelinks) and Q7101699 the label 'L'Orfeo' (Antonio Sartorio, 3 sitelinks); Swedish Wikipedia's 'L'Orfeo' redirects to the Monteverdi article, which opens 'Orfeo (italienska: L'Orfeo …)'. The Swedish front is now 'L'Orfeo', the same as the English, and a back note says 'Monteverdi's opera of 1607; Luigi Rossi and Antonio Sartorio also wrote Orfeo operas.' / 'Monteverdis opera från 1607; även Luigi Rossi och Antonio Sartorio skrev Orfeo-operor.' Evidence: Wikidata Q1118131 and Q7101699 with composer checks, Q724008's first performance 1607 with a check, English Wikipedia for both namesakes as verification. | fixed |
| deck | The description, method and selection said the works were chosen by how many Wikipedias cover them, but wikibase:sitelinks also counts Commons, Wikiquote, Wikisource and Wikinews. | Confirmed with the Wikidata API: Carmen has 74 sitelinks, 7 of them not Wikipedia; L'Orfeo and the Jupiter Symphony each have 35 including commonswiki. Counting Wikipedia articles only, 11 of the 83 works fall below 35 (lowest: Sonata Pathétique, 32 of 35), and one work outside the deck, La vie en rose (a song), has 34 of 34. The ranking was kept and the documentation corrected: description en 'chosen by how many Wikimedia sites (mostly language editions of Wikipedia) have a page on them', sv 'utvalda efter hur många Wikimedia-webbplatser (främst språkversioner av Wikipedia) som har en sida om dem'; method steps 2 and 4 and Selection say the count covers all Wikimedia projects and give the figures above. | fixed |
| deck | Namesake back notes were inconsistent: no note for Idomeneo (Galuppi), The Queen of Spades (Prokofiev) or Salome, and the Falstaff note omitted Elgar's Falstaff. | The namesake search was redone for the card fronts as used, labels and aliases (query 4), and one rule now applies to every card (method step 'Title clashes'): a back note names every musical namesake (opera, operetta, musical, ballet or concert work) by another composer with at least 5 sitelinks; films, TV, games, productions and popular songs are ignored. Under that rule notes were added or extended for falstaff (Elgar's symphonic study, 5 sitelinks, beside Salieri), aida (Elton John's musical, 19), bolero (Chopin's Boléro for piano, 9), salome (Antoine Mariotte's Salomé, 5), pastoral-symphony (Vaughan Williams, 10), manon-lescaut (Massenet's Manon, 29, which has the Swedish alias 'Manon Lescaut') and orfeo-ed-euridice (Haydn's L'anima del filosofo, 13, English alias 'Orfeo ed Euridice'), each with its Wikidata item and a composer check. No note for idomeneo: Galuppi's Idomeneo has 1 sitelink and Federici's 0. No note for the-queen-of-spades: Prokofiev's The Queen of Spades is film music with 2 sitelinks, and Suppé's operetta is titled Pique Dame, outside a same-title check. For salome the items the reviewer cited (Egisto Macchi, the Bizet item) are films, but query 4 found Mariotte's opera, now named. | fixed |
| pastoral-symphony | 'Pastoral Symphony' is also the usual name of Vaughan Williams's Symphony No. 3 (A Pastoral Symphony). | Confirmed: Wikidata Q256668, English label 'A Pastoral Symphony', aliases 'Symphony No. 3' and 'Pastoral Symphony', composer Ralph Vaughan Williams, 10 sitelinks. Back note now 'Symphony No. 6. Vaughan Williams's Symphony No. 3 is called A Pastoral Symphony.' / 'Symfoni nr 6. Vaughan Williams symfoni nr 3 kallas A Pastoral Symphony.', with Wikidata evidence and checks and English Wikipedia as verification. The Pifa in Messiah is a movement without its own namesake item matched by query 4 and is not named. | fixed |
| orfeo-ed-euridice | The method said the back is Wikidata's English label, but for Gluck the English label is 'Christoph Willibald von Gluck'; the card's form is an English alias. | Confirmed (Q130759: English label 'Christoph Willibald von Gluck', English alias and Swedish label 'Christoph Willibald Gluck', English and Swedish Wikipedia titles 'Christoph Willibald Gluck'). The method's Composers step now states the exception, and the card's Wikidata evidence says which form is the label and which the alias. | fixed |

### Round 2: Language and translation (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — independent Language and translation reviewer · **Scope:** All 83 cards: every front, back and note in the dossier and the built deck; doubtful Swedish titles and names checked against Swedish Wikipedia; the builder's read-only check run.

No language errors. One warning: the Swedish note on gianni-schicchi used the Italian 'Il trittico' although Swedish has 'Triptyken'. Five suggestions: the attested spelling 'Uvertyren 1812', idiomatic wording of the orfeo-ed-euridice note, Swedish punctuation and wording in the description, a 'balett' keyword, and documenting the language-tag convention for original-language titles. All were applied after checking Swedish Wikipedia.

| Card | Issue | Resolution | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| gianni-schicchi | The Swedish note 'Del av Il trittico.' uses the Italian title; Swedish has the established title Triptyken. | Confirmed: Swedish Wikipedia's article is 'Triptyken' and opens 'Triptyken (italiensk originaltitel Il trittico) är en samling av tre enaktsoperor'. Swedish note now 'Del av Triptyken (Il trittico).', with that article as evidence; the English note is unchanged. | fixed |
| 1812-overture | The Swedish front 'Ouvertyren 1812' is a Wikidata alias not found in Swedish Wikipedia's text, which uses 'Uvertyren 1812'. | Confirmed by Swedish Wikipedia full-text search: "Ouvertyren 1812" 0 hits, "Uvertyren 1812" 3 hits, including the article on Tchaikovsky ('de populära Serenad för stråkar och Uvertyren 1812 (båda 1880)', where it is also a link title). The Swedish front is now 'Uvertyren 1812', with that article as evidence; the Swedish label check, which tested the alias, was removed, and the method explains the change. | fixed |
| orfeo-ed-euridice | 'set the same title' / 'tonsatte samma titel' is unidiomatic: a composer sets a text, not a title. | Rewritten as 'Gluck's opera; Ferdinando Bertoni and others also wrote operas of this title, and Joseph Haydn's L'anima del filosofo is also known as Orfeo ed Euridice.' / 'Glucks opera; även Ferdinando Bertoni med flera skrev operor med samma titel, och Joseph Haydns L'anima del filosofo kallas också Orfeo ed Euridice.' (the Haydn clause comes from round 3's namesake check). | fixed |
| deck | The Swedish description used a spaced em dash, the unusual word 'Wikipediaupplagor' and the awkward 'Library of Congress auktoritetsregister'. | Swedish description now uses a spaced en dash, 'Wikimedia-webbplatser (främst språkversioner av Wikipedia)' (worded to match round 1's correction) and 'Library of Congress namnauktoriteter'.
